In the setting of $(\Box_{k})$, $\pi$ induces a strict isomorphism

$\hat{z}^{U}\simeq\mathrm{Spf}(\mathcal{O}_{U,z},\mathfrak{m}_{U,z})\simeq\mathrm{Spf}(\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{A}_{k}^{2},a},\mathfrak{m}_{\mathbb{A}_{k}^{2},a})\simeq\hat{a}^{\mathbb{A}_{k}^{2}}.$

In particular, since the ind-scheme formal completion commutes with arbitrary base change $\mathrm{Spec}\,A\to\mathrm{Spec}\,k$, from the base-changed diagram in $\mathsf{Sch}_{A}$

$\textstyle{\mathrm{Spec}\,A\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}$ $\scriptstyle{\mathrm{id}}$ $\scriptstyle{z_{A}}$ $\textstyle{\mathrm{Spec}\,A\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}$ $\scriptstyle{a_{A}}$ $\textstyle{D_{U_{A}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}$ $\scriptstyle{i_{A}}$ $\textstyle{\mathbb{A}_{A}^{1}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}$ $\scriptstyle{j_{A}}$ $\textstyle{U_{A}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}$ $\scriptstyle{\pi}$ $\textstyle{\mathbb{A}_{A}^{2}}$ $\textstyle{\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,(\Box_{A})}$

we get a strict isomorphism

$\widehat{z_{A}}^{U_{A}}\simeq\mathrm{Spf}(B\otimes_{k}A,J_{B_{A}})\simeq\mathrm{Spf}(A[x,y],\mathrm{I}_{A})\simeq\widehat{a_{A}}^{\mathbb{A}_{A}^{2}}.$

where $J_{B_{A}}$ is the ideal corresponding to the closed immersion $i_{A}\circ z_{A}:\mathrm{Spec}\,A\to U_{A}=\mathrm{Spec}(B\otimes_{k}A)$, and $\mathrm{I}_{A}$ the ideal corresponding to the closed immersion $j_{A}\circ a_{A}:\mathrm{Spec}\,A\to\mathbb{A}^{2}_{A}$.

paper.title: Two dimensional versions of the affine Grassmannian and their geometric description
paper.abstract: For a smooth affine algebraic group $G$ over an algebraically closed field, we consider several two-variables generalizations of the affine Grassmannian $G(\!(t)\!)/G[\![t]\!]$, given by quotients of the double loop group $G(\!(x)\!)(\!(y)\!)$. We prove that they are representable by ind-schemes if $G$ is solvable. Given a smooth surface $X$ and a flag of subschemes of $X$, we provide a geometric interpretation of the two-variables Grassmannians, in terms of bundles and trivialisation data defined on appropriate loci in $X$, which depend on the flag.
